notes: EMNLP 2018 CMU DoG dataset. 2 critic rounds (r1: 3 blockers -- false 'paper contradicts itself on turn counts' accusation, wrong 'shared document' scenario across 4 surfaces, unsupported split-holdout claim; r2 approve). Episode bf_emma 154.2 wpm, byte-verified.

Crafter (ICLR 2022, sole author Hafner). 3 critic rounds. r1: 4 blockers (Table A.1/B.1 conflation -- wrong agents on Wake Up, false 'only reward agent to place a furnace', wood rows quoted as stone rows, invented figcaption detail). r2: 2 new blockers -- the r1 fix introduced a false superlative and a false 'paper contradicts itself' charge, both from reading 1-decimal table rounding as true zeros; critic resolved them by parsing bar heights out of the PDF vector stream (Figures 6-7 are log-floored at 0.01%). r3: approve. Episode bm_daniel 157.9 wpm, byte-verified; its three added findings (Hafner co-authors Plan2Explore, score/return use different windows, human +/-6.8 is partition noise) were independently verified and two folded into the page.

PHYRE (NeurIPS 2019). 3 critic rounds, 12 blockers total -- all in interpretive prose; the critic independently cleared the AUCCESS definition, all 8 headline numbers, the MEM anomaly and all 6 edges in round 1. r1 (10): false 'every agent' quantifiers contradicted by the page's own table, an invented within-task feedback leak, OPTIMAL misused to justify budgets, 10k test vs 100k training budgets conflated, a mislabeled figcaption, an inverted reading of 4.4, 'roughly halves' for a 29.5% drop, a term ('interaction networks') absent from the paper, two wrong Figure 2 readings, and an over-scoped MEM claim. r2 (2): both fixes replaced a wrong claim with a differently-wrong one in the same spot -- resolved by deleting the brittle figure-recurrence count outright and re-anchoring the coverage sentence at a single x. r3: approve. Episode bf_emma 149.7 wpm, byte-verified; its added arithmetic and 4 PDF-sourced details independently checked.

SkillsBench (arXiv 2026-02, 78 authors). 2 critic rounds, 5 blockers: wrong model count (14 vs 15, and 14+3 != 18), a figcaption confusing a count with a ring percentage (53 Extended vs the 61% label), a FABRICATED edge to zhu-2025-agentic-benchmarks (S2 false positive, absent from the printed bibliography), a MISSED edge to koh-2024-visualwebarena (already a node; S2's record has no ArXiv externalId so arxiv-id-only matching dropped it -- and the builder then proposed it as a queue discovery), and an over-asserted takeaway contradicting the paper's own hedge. r2 approve after the critic independently title-matched the whole printed bibliography against all 610 nodes. Episode bm_fable 153.8 wpm, byte-verified.

HEAD-QA (ACL 2019). 2 critic rounds, 5 blockers: a false 'every real baseline beats the controls' that the page's own reprinted table refuted, an accuracy number leaking into a POINTS range, a claim that neural readers ran on Spanish (they only ever ran on HEAD-QA-EN), a false 'every strong system is neural' excluding the two IR baselines that actually win, and 'question 21' for 'image no. 21'. r2 approve; I then fixed two critic notes (a 3-vs-4 neural-system count the page contradicted itself on, and scoping the controls claim to the six-area average). Episode bf_lily 153.5 wpm, byte-verified; two of its added findings were verified and folded into the page -- BiDAF also falls under the Length control on the supervised split, and the controls are Spanish-only so every control-vs-neural comparison crosses languages.

JAMA Clinical Challenge + Medbullets (NAACL 2025, arXiv 2024-02). 2 critic rounds, 3 blockers -- the serious one an integrity error: the draft called the human raters 'physicians' across 13 surfaces incl. the node abstract and both meta descriptions, when the paper says Prolific crowdworkers screened for a Master's/Doctorate in Medicine/Healthcare at $12/hr. Also a false 'largest gap' superlative and a takeaway merging the two datasets' exceptions (MedAlpaca is Medbullets-only; JAMA's improver is Llama 2). r2 approve. Episode bm_daniel 160.1 wpm, byte-verified; it caught two of its own errors mid-render and flagged a correlation-magnitude error on the page (CTC Consistency -0.37 exceeds the quoted 0.32) which I verified and fixed, plus two transcription errors in tables.md.

Who did What (EMNLP 2016). 2 critic rounds, 4 blockers, all prose-level -- the page contradicted its own reprinted table ('well below' for a 0.01 gap), 'most' where the paper says 'many', a reversed direction ('closes' vs 'widens' the human/machine gap) in a sentence that contradicted its own appositive, and a wrong CBT description. Two risky builder calls both held up under 500-dpi coordinate verification: a reconstructed Table 3 column order and a §1-vs-§4 regime split (relaxed vs standard train). Queue net -1 -- no candidates worth adding, claim critic-verified. Episode bf_isabella 155.7 wpm, byte-verified; its anonymization-confound finding (only Attentive/Stanford were anonymized, and those are exactly the readers whose ranking flips) was verified and added to the critique.

PersonaMem (COLM 2025, arXiv 2025-04). 2 critic rounds, 7 blockers -- a reversed comparison across 4 surfaces (18% is BELOW the 25% floor, not 'barely above'), a false critique claim repeated 4x (RAG tested at 128k, not only 32k), an invented aggregation mechanism attributed to Appendix D.1, an altered quotation, a wrong benchmark count (3 not 2), a non-exhaustive ordering missing an exact 0.43 tie, and meta tags contradicting the body on persona count. I separately corrected the venue to COLM 2025 (PDF header on all 28 pages; DBLP had only CoRR), replaced 2 paraphrases sitting in quote marks with verbatim Figure 1 text, and fixed a second tables.md row shift verified at 900 dpi. Episode bm_fable 163.1 wpm, byte-verified 3 ways; its per-model split finding (12/15 below chance, and Claude-3.7-Sonnet last overall yet best on the hardest type) was verified at 900 dpi and added.

ToM-bAbI (EMNLP 2018). 2 critic rounds, 4 blockers: two MISSED inbound edges (QLoRA and BiGGen Bench both cite it -- the builder swept only the topical ToM cluster), a wrong story/question structure that contradicted the page's own takeaway (one question per test example, not four), 'had already solved bAbI' on six surfaces when the paper's own S4 says the best memory net fails 6 of 20 tasks under its joint training, and an altered quotation. r2 approve. tables.md was CLEAN for the first time in four papers -- the new column-anchoring check (a re-sum cannot catch a row shift) worked. Episode bf_alice 159.0 wpm, byte-verified 3 ways; its best-of-ten-runs finding (S5: MemN2N results are max-of-10 selections, which is why Figure 3's box plots sit far below the headline numbers) was verified and added to the critique. Queue net -1: the builder's only new candidate was already queued.

Ape210K (arXiv 2020-09, WITHDRAWN by its authors 2020-10-09). 3 critic rounds. r1: the page never mentioned the withdrawal, and its contamination row was premised on a public release; plus an invented causal claim, a false 'every prior SOTA model' quantifier, and a figure crop clipping the skip connection. r2: MY round-1 direction was wrong -- I over-read the withdrawal notice as 'never released', and the builder faithfully implemented it, so the page swung to asserting the dataset is unobtainable. It isn't: github.com/Chenny0808/ape210k (203 stars) has carried a full copy since 2020-10-13, four days after the withdrawal, and HuggingFace since 2023-05-22 (both verified by me). r3 approve on the accurate framing: official URL dead, third-party copy circulating, so leakage risk is LIVE and provenance is separately unverifiable. I verified the mirror's valid/test splits are 5,000 each, matching the paper. tables.md clean 2nd paper running. Episode bm_daniel 161.6 wpm, byte-verified 3 ways.

T-Eval (ACL 2024, arXiv 2023-12). 2 critic rounds. r1 (4): a false uniqueness claim the page's own table contradicted (Qwen-72B INSTRUCT-JSON 98.3 > GPT-4 95.9 is one of four counterexamples) traced to an interpretive gloss in tables.md; a spliced quotation; 4 missed outbound edges; and a missed inbound edge from BFCL recorded as unverifiable. r2 (1): the revision introduced a fresh false universal ('trails every comparison below' -- InternLM-20B actually ranks 6th of 18); I fixed that clause myself. Builder self-caught 2 false quantifiers before submitting and correctly withheld a paper-internal inconsistency. 34 edges, the largest batch this session, independently re-verified by the critic. tables.md clean 3rd paper running. Episode bf_lily 151.1 wpm, byte-verified; its INSTRUCT-inversion finding was verified and added, though I corrected its claim that INSTRUCT is Qwen-72B's worst ability (REASON is lower, 59.5 vs 63.1).

MedExQA (BioNLP@ACL 2024). 2 critic rounds, 6 blockers -- but ALL THREE of the builder's uniqueness claims survived exhaustive checking, a first in eleven papers. Blockers: a figcaption asserting what its own table refutes plus a nonexistent model (Meditron-13B; the family is Medinote), an inverted quantifier (Phi-2 was the exception, not the rule), GPT-4 listed under a logits-only header, a tie reported as a lead, one missed edge (Mistral-7B), and an unsupported 'independently written' provenance claim across 8 surfaces. Added the paper's own Limitations disclosure that the human eval was done by three of the authors at 5 samples/specialty with no IAA. tables.md clean 4th paper running. Episode bf_isabella 148.3 wpm, byte-verified 3 ways; it correctly reverted its own inject_podcast call rather than touching papers.json. Its finding that the paper never accounts for the SECOND explanation set -- the headline contribution -- was verified and is now the lead item in the critique.

GTA (NeurIPS 2024 D&B). 2 critic rounds, 4 blockers -- but all three counting claims held on first pass (2 of 16 clear 40%, the other 14 under 25% max 23.62, exactly 4 flat-zero ArgAcc), second paper running with clean quantifiers. Blockers: a bottom-line callout saying 'every other model under 25%' that four other surfaces on the same page contradicted (GPT-4o is 41.52); the REGIME TRAP sprung -- 89.55 Creativity F1 is END-TO-END, not step-by-step, so the takeaway's cross-regime contrast was built on a same-regime pair; 'four families' where the paper lists six; and an inverted size comparison (67B/70B called larger than 72B). I added a caveat that the replacement contrast (85.19 InstAcc vs 46.59 AnsAcc) spans two different metrics, since the benchmark reports none under both regimes. tables.md clean 5th paper running; all 15 edges correct first pass with a verified strong negative across 12 cluster papers. Episode bm_fable 154.4 wpm, byte-verified 3 ways; it avoided the regime trap entirely and did a least-squares voice regression over 618 episodes.

FollowIR (NAACL 2025, arXiv 2024-03; 8th queue-metadata correction -- queue said venue arXiv). 2 critic rounds, 9 blockers total: inverted Common Core sampling, a FABRICATED quotation, a 'not trained on retrieval data' qualifier applied to models it doesn't cover, five-vs-four model categories, a missed Codex edge, a SPURIOUS GPT-4 edge the report falsely claimed was bibliography-verified, a needed version-provenance note, a false 'largest gains anywhere' superlative, and then r2's B9 -- the B8 fix reversed a comparison the builder's own response file had stated correctly (Llama-3-8B's +5.07 exceeds FollowIR-7B's +2.1). I fixed B9 myself. I ALSO had to correct my own provenance note: the critic's B7 evidence (RR vs MRR, 'dozens per query') described arXiv v1, not the v3 the source link serves -- v3 matches the camera-ready on both, so I narrowed the note to the appendix-lettering difference I verified. Episode bf_emma 154.5 wpm, byte-verified 3 ways; its unescaped-'<' rendering flag was a false positive (HTML5 treats '<'+space as literal) but I escaped it anyway.

IntPhys 2019 (TPAMI 2022, arXiv 2018-03; 9th queue-metadata correction -- retitled between preprint and publication, queue said year 2018). 2 critic rounds, 4 blockers: one MISSED inbound edge (BIB), an inverted developmental timeline in a figcaption, shuffled-ID masks attributed to train instead of dev/test, and a false 'best-performing configuration' parenthetical. r2 approve -- and notably the B4 replacement (aggregated CNN identical to long-term CNN) was verified 192/192 cells, the first revision in four papers not to ship a fresh error. ROOT CAUSE of the missed edge, now in paper-builder.md: S2 keeps DUPLICATE records for retitled papers (2 extra CorpusIds, 69 unswept citers). Builder did excellent version work -- diffed arXiv v3 against the HAL manuscript (24/24 pages identical) rather than asserting, and correctly withheld a suspected paper inconsistency until the critic adjudicated it real. Episode bm_daniel 163.8 wpm, byte-verified; it caught that the page's 0.48-0.53 range was looser than the data (true range 0.48-0.52 across 15 cells) -- verified and tightened, and removed the tables.md gloss that seeded it.

DiscoveryWorld (NeurIPS 2024 D&B). 2 critic rounds, 8 blockers, two of them new failure modes: (1) the node's citation_count (82) leaked out of the hero facts strip into the prose as a claimed '82-point human/agent gap' -- the real figure is 43; (2) a real inbound citation from PaperBench was WRONGLY EXCLUDED because the citing PDF's text layer breaks the name as 'DIS- COVERYWORLD' -- the de-hyphenation rule applies to searching for a paper's name in a citing PDF, not just to quotations. Also: a procedure range that omitted Challenge, false exclusivity on 'the two hardest tasks' (three qualify), an 'in the 60s' characterization no cell supports, a false 'at best 8%' (ReAct reaches 10%), and an invented '1D' detail. Edges 9 -> 12. r2 approve with all four replacement claims verified clean. I separately fixed a gap-direction error the critic flagged as non-blocking (the gap NARROWS at Challenge, 53 -> 38 points) plus an unsupported latency claim and a typo. Episode bm_lewis 140.5 wpm, byte-verified; it discarded two renders after its own numeric audits, and its one page-level flag (a '32x32 tile grid' claim) was a false positive -- the paper states that verbatim.

Hi-ToM (EMNLP 2023 Findings). 2 critic rounds, 8 blockers -- including a THIRD fabricated quotation on this page ('structural costs' attributed to OpenToM, phrase absent from it), a false universal across 3 surfaces (all four models collapsing to zero before the top order -- false for GPT-4 at 0.45 and Claude at 0.30), 'near-perfect' extended to 1st order when the paper reserves it for 0th, an appended 'across all five categories' universal, a figcaption calling a deceptive message truthful, over-attributed run dates, and 4 missing edges. r2 approve; I then fixed a stale alt text still carrying the claim B1 removed. ROOT CAUSE recorded in paper-builder.md: a zero-hit grep is a claim about tooling first -- three mechanisms have each produced false 'not cited' results (line-broken names, small-caps, and embedded NUL bytes). S2's citation list for this paper matched ZERO nodes despite four real citers. I scanned all 86 work/*/paper.txt and stripped NUL bytes from 4 of them, which had been silently breaking grep. Episode bm_fable 159.9 wpm, byte-verified; it independently re-verified the OpenToM quote and noted an abstract-only check would have produced a false negative.

AgentDAM (NeurIPS 2025). 2 critic rounds, 6 blockers: a figure caption misreading Figure 5 as evaluation-run stability when it is dataset-construction elbow evidence; two missed edges (CoT, tau-bench); a dedupe failure where report.json proposed tau-bench as a NEW candidate though yao-2024-tau-bench is already a node AND a missed edge; an axis conflation ('every number in Tables 3-5 flows through the judge' -- utility comes from a binary env reward); and an invented 'GPT-based' attribution. r2 left one residual: the B1 fix said leakage is HIGHEST at one sample per seed when it is LOWEST (curves rise into the plateau) -- I verified against the paper's own 'high variance and lower performance' and fixed it. Builder self-caught 2 false superlatives and 3 quotation issues before submitting; all three of its universal claims held row-by-row. tables.md self-certified one false claim (representation splice is text-only for BOTH Llamas) -- corrected, never reached the page. Episode bf_isabella 159.5 wpm, byte-verified; its finding that Llama-3.3-70B generated the benchmark's user_data AND is one of the six graded agents was verified and added to the critique.

EQ-Bench (arXiv 2023-12, sole author). 2 critic rounds, 8 blockers: the best-of-two protocol misdescribed as two independent runs (it is first-pass vs post-critique from ONE administration), n=25 where the SECEU overlap is 9, two models cited in a correlation pool they aren't in, an invented cost argument attributed to the paper, invented dialogue specifics, a 3-vs-4 checkpoint count, a softened table discrepancy, and then r2's B8 on the correlation n's. Builder correctly withheld nothing this time -- the appendix discrepancy WAS on the page and its report wrongly said otherwise. RESOLVED A CONFLICT MYSELF: the episode claimed AlpacaEval n=8, the critic said 7; computing Pearson directly settles it -- 8 rows carry both scores but the printed 0.91 only reproduces at n=7 (r=0.9054); including Mistral-7B gives 0.799, and its AlpacaEval cell 54.52 is identical to its ARC cell. Added that to the page so a reader can check it. Also corrected tables.md's Table 6 count (11 models x 3 = 33 rows, not 10 x 30). Episode bf_emma ~157 wpm, byte-verified.

LegalAgentBench (ACL 2025, arXiv 2024-12; 10th queue-metadata correction -- queue said arXiv 2024). 2 critic rounds, 4 blockers. BEST BUILDER RUN OF THE SESSION: it independently found THREE paper claims that don't hold (the 'gap can reach 65%' -- true max 47.5; 'GLM-4-Plus surpasses GPT-4o across all tasks' -- loses 5 of 18 cells; 'all baselines decreased as hops increased' -- 13 of 24 rows non-monotonic), used the weaker true statement in each case, reported rather than asserted, AND caught its own directional error mid-draft. All three adjudicated correct by the critic. Blockers: the two figures were under each other's captions; the process rate was described as reading the trajectory on 5 surfaces when it scores the same final-answer text as success rate (proved by arithmetic -- process falls BELOW success at 5-hop, impossible under a trajectory scan); and a missed edge to liu-2023-llm-p that was in S2's refs AND the printed bibliography. r2 caught a HALF-APPLIED FIX: after the builder swapped images and I relabelled captions and in-text refs, the alt attributes were left inverted. Added a neutral 65%-vs-47.5 note and a parenthetical that the paper names the metric both 'process rate' and 'progress rate'. Episode bm_daniel 159.1 wpm, byte-verified; it caught 3 of its own drafting errors before rendering.

PhotoChat (ACL 2021). 2 critic rounds, 3 blockers: an INVERTED filter condition (the page stated the margin test as the requirement when footnote 2 makes it the disqualifier), two more invented specifics ('a coffee cup' for black tea; 'confuses puffins with a duck after keying on atlantic' inverting the paper's double 'fails to'), and the disputed 58.1 superlative asserted in the page's own voice on 5 surfaces. Builder correctly withheld BOTH suspected inconsistencies and caught 2 of its own queue candidates as already-queued. The critic then settled the 58.1-vs-58.9 question decisively by extracting PDF FONT RUNS: Table 2 bolds each column max, marking T5-3B's 58.9 as best F1 while the prose headlines 58.1. Page now attributes rather than asserts, and reproduces the paper's bolding in both reprinted tables so a reader sees it. Episode am_puck 154.8 wpm, byte-verified; it found a FIFTH grep false-negative mechanism -- fi/fl LIGATURES, present in 43 of 90 extracted texts -- now recorded in paper-builder.md alongside line-broken names, small-caps, NUL bytes and spaced multiplication signs.

COLM 2025; 2 critic rounds, 7 blockers r1 (self-contradicting recall table, two false quantifier ranges, metric/row swap, false 'every benchmark' claim, 2 missed edges); approve r2. 628 nodes / 6833 edges. Podcast bm_lewis 27m30s.

COLM 2024 (13th metadata correction, OpenReview-confirmed; S2/DBLP say arXiv 2023). 2 critic rounds, 1 blocker r1: page scoped universals over Table 3's 19 rows as the whole evaluation, missing Table 8's 6 further combos and the StarCoderBase-1b reversal (4.90 descr vs 5.48 lazy) - true count 24/25. 629 nodes / 6848 edges. Podcast bf_lily 25m27s.

NeurIPS 2023 MATH-AI workshop (venue independently confirmed). 2 critic rounds, 7 blockers r1 + 2 in newly-written r1-fix prose (Table 8 '6 of 8' fraction that was really two columns' FN counts; a raster estimate printed as exact 62.7%) + 1 note (Table 2 range understated 3-6 vs true 3-12) - all 3 fixed by hand. B1 was a 7th false-negative mechanism: S2 null-stub reference record + post-publication retitling. B2 added the evaluations tag (rubric grader is a co-headline contribution per the abstract). 630 nodes / 6885 edges. Podcast af_bella 29m30s.

EMNLP 2024 (14th metadata correction; confirmed 3 ways). 2 critic rounds, 4 blockers r1: false 'only benchmark with both ticks' (MLAgentBench also qualifies); invented 'five files' count; grading tolerance attached to tables when the paper grants it only to charts; 3 missed edges from S2 null-stub references (12 of 32 refs were stubs, MLAgentBench absent entirely). Page's 3 claims-against-the-paper all verified and kept. 631 nodes / 6901 edges. Podcast am_fenrir 30m24s.

Findings of ACL 2026 (15th metadata correction; DBLP conf/acl/ZhangZCLYWDHTY26). 2 critic rounds, 9 blockers r1 + 1 new defect in the r1-fix prose. Notable: Figure 1's inlined image was a crop of the whole page-1 title block (extract_figures.py bug on two-column first pages - spawned task_8de53566); 23-model averages attached to individual models; GPT-4o's 9-column sweep unscoped while appendix Table 5 has it losing 3; CR rubric mis-stated to inflate the critique. Added the paper's own Tables 5/6 contamination split (81.81 BCB vs 24.32 curated). 632 nodes / 6916 edges. Podcast bf_emma 27m06s.

arXiv 2025 (v2 Apr); no venue correction - only an ACL ARR submission and a CVPR 2026 workshop poster exist. 2 critic rounds, 4 blockers r1: missed CoT edge (S2 null stub; builder matched by arXiv id instead of surname+year as instructed); a superlative falsified by its own table's Human row (96.81 vs 11.34); a figure caption attributing 5 task-category shares to 4 scene sources; a non-verbatim quotation. Builder caught and re-cropped 2 mis-cropped figures using the warning added after DataSciBench. 633 nodes / 6928 edges. Podcast bf_alice 26m12s.

arXiv 2025 (16th metadata correction: queue said year 2026, arXiv 2505 = May 2025). 81 authors, elided per liang-2022-helm convention. 2 critic rounds, 6 blockers r1; round 2 clean. All 3 of the page's claims-against-the-paper upheld, incl. that the abstract's '40% lower computational cost' is unsupported by its own tables (40 occurs exactly once in the paper; every candidate reading lands 8-17%). Blockers: 2 superlatives falsified by another row of the same table, a false quantifier the paper itself contradicts one sentence later, a false 'contamination not discussed anywhere' (p.3 fn.1), a count bound to the wrong object, and the missing evaluations tag (adjudicated in the critic's favour). bibliography.tsv artifact worked - 27 refs confirmed as the real count in seconds. 634 nodes / 6934 edges. Podcast bf_isabella 27m06s.

arXiv 2025; no venue correction (SEA @ NeurIPS 2025 workshop poster + ACL ARR submission only). 2 critic rounds, 8 blockers r1 - the most since DataSciBench; round 2 clean. Two of the builder's four accusations against the paper were WRONG (the 80% search-validity pushback ignored Table 4; the Table 6 'discrepancy' is the paper's own documented Travel-22/33/44 choice-ablation subset). Also: a total reported as an active figure (27.32 vs 24.06 - the exact nesting collapse), a caption falsified by the figure the page inlines, a superlative false on 2 columns of the same table, 2 bad quotations (a hybrid and a dropped word), and an invented provenance. Builder ran git checkout on papers.json mid-draft and self-reported; verified nothing lost. 635 nodes / 6947 edges. Podcast bm_fable 25m51s.

17th metadata correction, and the most interesting one: venue arXiv -> NEJM AI (vol 2 issue 9, 2025-08-28), resolved via Crossref from a DOI found in the CITING paper's bibliography. Neither DBLP, OpenReview nor S2 had it; the paper carries three different titles across arXiv/DBLP/NEJM. 2 critic rounds, 3 blockers r1: a missed edge (shao-2026-medagentsbench cites this; the builder's grep on the OTHER paper's text hit the hyphenation false negative - reverse-direction sweeps need the same normalization), a false 'no format repair' accusation (the harness does strip tool_code fences), and an invented specific attributing the graders to the two named physicians. Round 2 clean. 636 nodes / 6952 edges. Podcast bm_daniel 22m54s.

CoRL 2019, 1724 citations - most-cited paper this pipeline has processed. Queue reprioritized before this paper (head had drifted to 40-cite entries while 74 >=100-cite entries waited). arXiv PDF serves v2 (2021) which says it updates the CoRL manuscript but carries no itemized changelog - verified by full-text sweep. 2 critic rounds, 3 blockers r1: a factual error claiming ML10 and ML45 share a train/test split (the held-out fives are disjoint and ML10's test tasks are ML45 training tasks), plus TWO false accusations against the paper - a mis-stated MT50 'internal tension' the paper explains in Figure 16's caption, and a 'no variance reported' claim falsified by Appendix C's n=10 seed-sensitivity bands. Round 2 clean. The episode agent then found a real paper defect both builder and critic missed: p.7's prose inverts the MAML/RL2 pairing for ML10 test (Table 1 says MAML 31.6, RL2 35.8) while the ML45 sentence one line later is correct - added to the page. 637 nodes / 6959 edges. Podcast af_bella 29m35s.

IJCV 2020, 1631 citations. NO metadata correction - I wrongly told the builder the queue said year 2018 (inferred from the arXiv id instead of reading the entry, which already said 2020/IJCV 2020); the builder caught it. 2 critic rounds, 3 blockers r1: a FABRICATED 'on shared classes' restriction on the 17.4x box-count claim, in 3 places incl. the node abstract - and the fabrication inverts the picture, since the adjacent Table 6 column (Open Images All, 200 classes) has 4.8x FEWER boxes than COCO; a visual-relationship criterion misstated twice in one clause (same-class + 20% overlap, vs the real different-classes + 20% enlargement); and a figure alt/caption that misdescribed the chart above it. Round 2 clean. First use of the new report.json accusations block: all 4 accusations verified TRUE and the critic audited the searches rather than re-deriving, catching one gap (a p.18 mitigation the builder missed). Episode was re-rendered after the agent self-caught a fabricated citation-behaviour claim; Cloudflare serves the superseded render at the canonical URL until the 4h TTL expires - origin and feed are correct. 638 nodes / 6964 edges. Podcast bf_emma 29m23s.

NeurIPS 2023, 1255 citations. 2 critic rounds, 3 blockers r1: a wrong comparison set ('best FWT of all five algorithms' when MTL's FWT/NBT cells are literally blank - only 4 report it); a real paper defect the builder had chosen not to assert (Figure 1's box captions are swapped relative to both S4.2 and the thumbnails inside those boxes, verified at 300dpi) - now named on the page; and an invented CORA contents list. Round 2 clean. Second use of the accusations block and the first fully-clean audit: all 3 claims true and all 3 rebuttal searches independently re-verified. The builder also correctly AVOIDED a false edge - LIBERO cites ref [59] in-text as 'SuperGLUE' but the printed entry is Sarlin et al.'s SuperGlue feature-matching paper. 639 nodes / 6971 edges. Podcast bm_lewis 35m07s.

IEEE RA-L 2020, 996 citations. Real metadata correction, verified by reading the queue entry: it said year 2019 alongside venue 'IEEE RA-L 2020'. 2 critic rounds + 1 hand fix. The load-bearing finding held under exhaustive check: arXiv v1 has NO experiments/results/evaluation section under any heading, no table environment, no numeric result in any figure or caption - it is a pure benchmark proposal, so the page is built around Figure 7's histograms and the few-shot protocol. Version caveat scoped throughout (arXiv v1 preprint only; the RA-L camera-ready is inaccessible). Blockers: an invented 'three-to-fifty-task benchmarks were the norm' range (the paper prints exactly one prior task count); a 'four of the five' count that contradicted the page's own body text (it's five of five); and two fabricated Figure 4 strings. Round 2 found one regression caused by the r1 fix (the maroon variation called 'its fourth' when Figure 4 shows an ellipsis before variation V) - fixed by hand. 3rd accusations-block run, all 5 true and searches adequate. Bidirectional Meta-World edge verified genuine: RLBench cites Meta-World's project website, which predates its arXiv posting. 640 nodes / 6987 edges. Podcast bm_fable 20m48s.

arXiv-only, 707 citations. No metadata correction needed (queue already correct). 2 critic rounds, 7 blockers r1 - the most on any paper this run; round 2 clean. The distinctive finding survived: arXiv v3 (Jan 2025) contradicts itself, with the Abstract describing 'our new release robosuite v1.5' while S1 scopes the reported results to 'the v1.0 robosuite release'. B3 was partly my error - my brief said 2 versions when there are 3 (v2 2022-11-15), and the builder sharpened my imprecise framing into a false claim that most citations accrued against v1; true split across the three windows is ~18/37/41 percent of 707. Other blockers: a Figure 4 misread (Panda led 5 of 9, not 'nearly every task'), a false 'the one task' quantifier, an invented 'UT Austin' attribution (the word appears nowhere; only Stanford PAIR is named), a misstated training protocol, a false Spot-commercial-availability claim, and an unsupported claim that the environments expose no success signal (p.4 documents that they do). Builder correctly avoided a false SAC edge - robosuite cites arXiv 1812.05905, not the node's 1801.01290. 641 nodes / 6994 edges. Podcast bf_isabella 21m59s.

ACL 2020, 489 citations. Builder was killed mid-build by an API stall and resumed from transcript; no data was lost (graph was untouched). Deliberate date exception: date='2020-07' not the arXiv month, because the arXiv posting (2021-06-30) POSTDATES the ACL publication by a year - S2 publicationDate 2020-07-01, and every ACL-2020 node in the corpus has date <= venue year. backfill_dates.py would try to undo this; recorded in report.json. 2 critic rounds, 6 blockers r1 + 6 hand-applied notes after approval. Builder work that held up: its own verbatim-quote audit was verified complete (34 quotes), all four hand re-crops correct after the extractor mis-cropped two and missed one entirely, and the edge sweep complete in both directions. 644 nodes / 7030 edges. Podcast bf_lily 29m21s.

MLSys 2020, 392 citations, 37 authors (elided). A SYSTEMS benchmark - measures time-to-train to a fixed quality target, not model capability - which made the capability-vs-systems frame the page's whole job. 2 critic rounds, 7 blockers r1; round 2 clean. The builder DECLINED the benchmarks tag, arguing the rubric is LLM-scoped; I adjudicated against it on precedent I verified myself (tay-2020-long-range-arena is tagged and likewise ranks architectures for efficiency, not capability; TREC-QA/LFW/CIFAR/CelebA/OpenImages show LLM-era scoping isn't enforced; Gym/ALE/RLBench show 'not a dataset' isn't disqualifying; and the queue entry itself says survey=benchmarks role=core). evaluations correctly declined. Blockers included a FABRICATED author affiliation (Baidu, on 5 surfaces - every Baidu mention in the paper is the DeepBench citation), the node abstract wrong for the THIRD consecutive paper, and one of the builder's own accusations that didn't survive (demanding the 1.3x be decomposed into a hardware-scale component that is zero by construction). First use of the new surfaces_checked artifact: all 7 blockers, all 7 surfaces, and the critic audited 4 entries end-to-end and found every file+line citation exact. Both verified and fixed. Builder found NO core queue candidates. 645 nodes / 7039 edges. Podcast bm_daniel 26m09s.

S2's reference list for this record is literally null, so the 73-ref hand parse was the only path to out-edges; incoming swept across BOTH records (525-citer union). 2 critic rounds, 6 blockers r1 + 1 regression r2 (which the critic owned as its own r1 fix_hint propagated - '35 newly acquired scene types' where the paper counts 35 scenes and Table 1 gives 8 types). Blockers: survey population inverted (fifty responses PER ACTIVITY, not per respondent); related-work groups inverted with 2 reattributed quotes and an invented gloss; Table 3 called monotonic when Kin. Dis. goes 0.00->12.34->10.82; a fabricated 'an unprecedented' quote; the Table 4 ablation merged across populations on FOUR surfaces incl. the node abstract (RL-Prim. only, 42-77%, not 42-88%); and a wrong Figure 5 denominator. Second use of surfaces_checked - all 6 blockers, all 7 surfaces, critic spot-checked and every n/a true. The episode agent then caught TWO errors in MY brief (I mis-assigned Figure 5's 44% to grasping when the legend puts it on Policy, and said ~35 authors from the 2024 version when CoRL lists 28) - the page was already right on both. 646 nodes / 7054 edges. Podcast bf_isabella 30m00s.

CVPR 2024, 356 citations, non-arXiv (CVF source). 2 critic rounds, 7 blockers r1; round 2 clean. evaluations tag ADDED on the critic's ruling, overruling the builder: the paper numbers 'Evaluation' as a contribution, Fig 1 says 'our proposed LLM-Match metric', S5 is titled 'Human Alignment and Robustness of LLM-Match' - and decisively, liu-2024-mmbench (the protocol OpenEQA adapts) itself carries evaluations, as do 62 of 151 evaluations papers dual-tagged. Blockers: a non-monotone 'weakest to strongest' ordering, a false universal the paper's own observation 5 contradicts, 'consistently' for the paper's 'generally' plus an increase called a drop, a false accusation about the abstract, and the node abstract labelling question counts as scan counts (missed surface #5 in a row). B1's missed in-edge (li-2024-embodied-agent-interface) was invisible from OpenEQA's side because BOTH papers' S2 reference lists are publisher-elided - a one-directional sweep is structurally blind there. The builder's zero-hit result across ten embodied-AI nodes was verified correct (critic re-derived 54 refs and swept 356 citers five ways). Episode agent then caught THREE errors in my brief: 24 authors not ~19, six affiliations not three, and - importantly - the paper DOES claim 'the first open-vocabulary benchmark' four times including unqualified, where I told it the paper doesn't. It also surfaced that the 86.8 human ceiling rests on TWO participants (S3, verbatim), which the page never said; I verified and added it, since that is half the headline gap. 647 nodes / 7064 edges. Podcast bf_alice 26m40s.
Fixed at verify: '18 extractive datasets' -> 18 QA datasets (page+node); Figure 1 blue series is 'Best result' not D-Net (RACE bar 53.9 = Delphi; macro 68.9 = D-Net -> one cell inconsistent).

3 critic rounds. r1: invented reconciliation of the 400-vs-389 contradiction, unsupported 'most benchmarks skip' claim, wrong MTLC range that had also reached the node abstract, mis-cropped figure. r2: B2's fix leaked the priority claim onto the zero-shot split. r3 (fix written by orchestrator): approved. Episode agent then found two further paper defects, both verified and added to the critique: LH-MTLC cells 0.08%/0.17% are arithmetically incompatible with the stated 1,000-chain denominator, and the conclusion restates the priority claim without its hedge and with unseen environments folded in.

2 critic rounds. r1: fabricated quotation (two paper sentences blended inside one set of quote marks), an asserted total absence the paper does contradict, wrong datasets in the contamination row, plus two promoted items - the page disagreed with itself on the excluded-model count (four vs five; five is right) and tables.md overclaimed that all Table 6 rows re-sum. Episode agent then found a third undercount: GPT-4o beats HPE on 3 of 7 OE zero-shot dimensions, not 2 (Instruction Alignment 80 vs 60 was missed) - verified and fixed. Also corrected the tables.md RM denominator (20 trials, not 1,000 chains; all 15 cells are multiples of 1/20) and normalized DynamiCrafter spelling. Tagged evaluations in addition to benchmarks: the rubric explicitly permits both, and Implicit Manipulative Evaluation is a genuinely novel protocol.

2 critic rounds, 6 blockers in r1. Root cause of the headline blocker was in tables.md: Table V's 8 columns were read as '4 Success then 4 Grasp' when they interleave per task, which put the wrong task name (Put Eggplant, not Put Carrot on Plate) on the page. Fixed at source and re-verified against PDF x-coordinates. Other blockers: false metric-scope claim, superlatives Table IV contradicts, a wrong cell (0.087 vs 0.142), merged sample sizes across four surfaces, overstated correlation ceiling. Episode agent then flagged three items: a genuine Table I vs Tables IV/XII drawer-column inconsistency in the paper (verified, added to critique + tables.md), an unsupported 'paired' gloss on the ~1500-episode figure (fixed across four surfaces), and a claim that SIMPLER doesn't cite Meta-World -- that one was wrong, the paper spells it 'Meta-world' at reference [73], so the edge stands. Tagged evaluations in addition to benchmarks: MMRV is a new metric and validated real-to-sim proxy evaluation is a new paradigm.

2 critic rounds, 3 blockers in r1: a nine-vs-eight row count on Table 3 (the 9 traced to tables.md's own flagged-but-used guess), a takeaway comparing against the wrong baseline where the correct baseline would have undercut its own thesis, and a truncated figure whose caption described rows the image didn't contain. Episode agent then found the abstract's third headline number - 'a 10.9% gain in code generation success rate' - appears exactly once in the paper and derives from nothing in Table 1 (like-for-like pairings give 14.7 and 7.4; all-variant means give 9.5). Verified and added to the critique, alongside a wording fix: the 367/228% figures are configuration averages over four tasks, not a single cell. Also replaced tables.md's 'rounding noise' diagnosis of the ACT/DP Average-row mismatch with an explicit 'unexplained, do not diagnose' - rounding cannot explain it, since the other six columns round correctly. Declined evaluations: this is a generator + suite, not a new way to evaluate.

2 critic rounds, 6 blockers in r1 - three of them summary-surface-only (dek/meta/og/node abstract correct nowhere, body correct everywhere): a nine-tasks-vs-four-benchmarks conflation that also claimed a clean GPT-3.5 sweep the paper loses twice, a 'most of the gap' that is 43.2%, and a dek making MMedBench pair a corpus with itself. Plus a table mislabelling GPT-4 (5-shot, CoT) as zero-shot (source was tables.md, since fixed and annotated), a nonexistent zero-shot regime for the MMed models, and a three-vs-four metric count. Episode agent then found two substantive items, both verified and added to the critique: Table 1's zero-shot GPT-4 average (74.27) does not reconcile with the mean of its own six cells (75.31) while every other row reconciles within 0.02; and the six language columns are not the same task - French test is 48.39% multiple-correct where four other languages are 0%, Russian is processed into binary choice (50% floor), and test splits run 199 to 3,426 under an unweighted macro-mean. Declined evaluations: a rationale-annotated benchmark plus a corpus and models, not a new way to evaluate.

3 critic rounds. r1: an invented score-quantization mechanism (the page inferred that 4-seed percentage scores could only take 5 discrete values, but no experiment is both percentage-scored and 4-seed - most score continuous normalized regret) and a baseline-vintage claim of 'all pre-2017' contradicted by the paper's own 2018 prior-functions citation, across five surfaces. Promoted quote drift in four places to a blocker. r2 closed both but introduced a fifth drifted quotation ('for 10k episodes' appears nowhere; the paper says 'after'). r3 (fix written by orchestrator) approved. My brief was wrong on two counts and the builder caught both: S2's reference list has 16 entries with no externalIds including mis-parsed body text, not 'zero null stubs' - my check tested only for a missing title - and my edge pass missed brockman-2016-openai-gym (absent from S2 entirely) and chollet-2019-measure-of-intelligence (S2 truncates the title). Tagged evaluations alongside benchmarks.

3 critic rounds, 7 blockers in r1 - the most on one paper. Three were the page contradicting itself (SPECTER credited with beating baselines it trails; Table 2's significance markers read backwards; 'every variant' where PALs is 69.9). Others: wrong per-format split, reversed direction on 69.0 vs 69.1, wrong count and colour description on the SciDocs block, and a 'baselines frozen at submission' claim contradicted by E5-v2/Instructor/Ada-002 all postdating v1 and being evaluated. r2 closed six but the B2 fix inverted the polarity again; r3 (fix written by orchestrator) approved. The markers inverted twice in review, so I re-derived them from the PDF vector layer myself and rewrote tables.md's marker note from the rules (In-Train x=386.9-402.6 has an underline only at y=275.5, the ensemble row) - the old note read as though 62.9 were not underlined, which is what misled the episode agent into proposing a wrong 'fix'. Episode agent also found a genuine third prose/table mismatch, verified and added: the paper says adapter variants beat MTL CTRL overall with Fusion best, but PALs (an adapter variant per the caption) trails MTL CTRL on all three columns and Fusion ties Adapters at every digit while costing 22M params/format against 1M.

2 critic rounds, 5 blockers in r1: a >50-point drop misattributed to BERT/RoBERTa when the paper's subject is SMN/DAM (and arithmetically impossible for BERT), a twelve-vs-thirteen dataset count stated twice with two mutually inconsistent lists, two node-abstract defects (taxonomy scope, and MuTual-plus's purpose stated backwards), an overstated Table 5 flatness claim (1.9 points is the endpoint delta; the full bucket range is 16.9), and two comparatives contradicted by their own tables. Promoted the bolding suggestion: the page had led with the smallest of four discrepancies. Episode agent then found the sharpest item on the page: six MRR cells in Table 3 are arithmetically impossible given their own R@1/R@2 with four candidates. I re-derived the bound over every row - all six transformer rows and Human sit inside it (RoBERTa 0.836 in [0.830,0.839]; Human 0.964 in [0.962,0.964]), which validates the bound, while Random prints 0.604 against a ceiling of 0.542 despite R@1/R@2 being exactly the theoretical 0.250/0.500, and Dual LSTM's test MRR 0.743 exceeds its own R@2 of 0.491. Added to the critique, narrowed the MuTual-plus argument onto DAM's recall numbers (two of its three legs sat on infeasible cells), and recorded both findings in tables.md along with a rewrite of its Table 4 bolding note, which had contradicted its own cell listings and carried a stray thinking artifact.

3 critic rounds, 13 blockers total - the most of any paper in this run. The dominant failure was sentences contradicted by numbers printed in the same sentence (4 of the 10 round-1 blockers), including a blanket 'improves every retriever tested' where GritLM-written reasoning queries lower 7 of 13. That one survived into round 2 in a second form (Llama-3-70B lowers GritLM 21.0 to 20.9) and I then fixed only one of its two surfaces before catching the takeaway. The page's central finding held throughout and was confirmed independently: the paper states its ceiling as 24.3 nDCG@10 in three places while Table 2's own Avg. column tops out at 22.5. Builder also corrected my own edge list in both directions (dropped a HellaSwag false positive, added BEIR). Episode agent then supplied two verified strengthenings, both added: Table 42's k=10 to k=100 reranking average conceals a domain inversion (Biology 26.1 to 42.5 and Psychology 32.6 to 42.1 against LeetCode 24.5 to 5.6 and AoPS 8.9 to 2.4), and Appendix Table 12 shows the contamination result is epoch 10 of a run that swings 4.9 points and exceeds its own baseline at epoch 9. Declined evaluations - a dataset/suite contribution whose analyses apply existing methods.

3 critic rounds, 6 blockers. Two were column-position misreads of the same class: Table 4's consultation-stage row was read one column left (30.09% belongs to treatment principles, not diagnosis process, and the paper's own prose says so), and Table 7's JianPeiGPT Average was initially taken from the Graduate-Entrance-Exam cell - the builder caught that one itself pre-draft. Also: an invented reconciliation of the 174-vs-176 category discrepancy that the builder's own tables.md had explicitly warned against, a body-vs-takeaway contradiction on professions, and a misquote. Round 2 opened two new blockers caused by the revision, one of which traces to a round-1 suggestion of the critic's that I promoted to must-fix without verifying it: the claim that AntGLM-Med's Average was the only one in either table that fails to re-derive is false (Sunsimiao-7B's three-shot Average misses by 5.71 against AntGLM-Med's 2.33, and a plain non-asterisked Mistral row misses by 2.04), which collapsed the inference built on it. Replaced with the paper's own Appendix C statement that all three commercial models' results were vendor-submitted after CMB opened - direct evidence rather than inference. Episode agent found no errors but supplied two additions, both verified and added: Table 10's 2-gram keyword comparison (CMB-TCM vs MedQA-USMLE, zero overlap) is measured support for the localization thesis the page argued from prose, and the paper's own finding that TCM subcategories always score lowest closes its premise's loop.
